UNIVERSAL PROFESSIONAL CHARACTER SHEET — IDENTITY & OUTFIT LOCK

REFERENCE IMAGE — IDENTITY PRESERVATION

Use the uploaded reference image as the primary and authoritative reference for the character.

Analyze the reference image carefully and preserve the exact identity of the person, including facial structure, eyes, nose, lips, eyebrows, skin tone, age, hairstyle, hair color, hair texture, body proportions, and all distinctive physical features.

The character must remain immediately recognizable as the exact same person in every panel.

If the reference image contains a male character, preserve the same male character. If it contains a female character, preserve the same female character.

Do not change the person's identity, gender presentation, facial features, body proportions, or natural appearance.

OUTFIT & STYLING LOCK

Reproduce the exact outfit shown in the reference image, including:

Clothing design, color, fabric, texture, and fit.
Neckline, sleeves, collar, buttons, embroidery, patterns, and decorative details.
Shoes, jewelry, watches, belts, bags, and other visible accessories.
Hairstyle, makeup, and other styling details where applicable.

Do not redesign, replace, simplify, or add clothing elements. If the reference image shows a full outfit, preserve the complete outfit consistently across all views.

CHARACTER SHEET LAYOUT — PROFESSIONAL 3 × DETAIL GRID

Create one premium, photorealistic character reference sheet inspired by professional fashion lookbooks, costume design boards, and cinematic production character sheets.

Use a clean, organized multi-panel layout with thin white divider lines, a neutral dark-grey studio background, consistent studio lighting, and elegant black information strips with small, refined white serif labels.

PANEL 1 — FRONT VIEW
Full-body, straight-on view of the character standing naturally. Show the complete outfit from head to toe, including footwear. Keep the face clearly visible.

PANEL 2 — SIDE VIEW
Full-body side or three-quarter profile view of the exact same character. Preserve the identical face, hairstyle, outfit, accessories, and body proportions.

PANEL 3 — BACK VIEW
Full-body rear view showing the back of the hairstyle, clothing construction, seams, fabric, silhouette, and footwear.

PANEL 4 — FACE CLOSE-UP
A high-resolution close-up of the character's face, showing realistic skin texture, natural pores, eyes, eyebrows, nose, lips, and hairstyle.

PANEL 5 — EYES CLOSE-UP
A detailed close-up of the character's eyes and eyebrows, preserving the exact eye shape, eye color, and surrounding facial features.

PANEL 6 — LIPS & FACIAL DETAILS
A close-up of the lips and lower facial area. For male characters, retain the exact beard, mustache, and facial hair if present. For female characters, preserve the natural lip shape and makeup shown in the reference.

PANEL 7 — OUTFIT DETAILS
Show close-up views of the most important clothing details, such as collars, buttons, embroidery, stitching, lace, sequins, decorative patterns, pockets, or garment construction.

PANEL 8 — ACCESSORIES & FOOTWEAR
Show the actual accessories and shoes from the reference image. If accessories are absent, use additional relevant outfit-detail shots instead.

PANEL 9 — FABRIC & MATERIAL TEXTURE
Show a macro-level detail of the actual clothing material, including realistic weave, folds, stitching, embroidery, shine, transparency, or surface texture as applicable.

COMPOSITION & CAMERA CONSISTENCY

Keep the same character identity across every panel.
Maintain consistent body proportions and physical appearance.
Use realistic full-body photography with correct anatomy.
Keep front, side, and back views anatomically consistent.
Use the same neutral grey studio environment throughout.
Use soft, professional studio lighting and natural shadows.
Maintain realistic skin texture and highly detailed clothing materials.
Ensure the full body, head, hands, legs, and shoes are not accidentally cropped in the three main views.
Separate every panel with clean, thin white borders.
Add minimal, correctly spelled labels: FRONT VIEW, SIDE VIEW, BACK VIEW, FACE CLOSE-UP, EYES CLOSE-UP, OUTFIT DETAILS, ACCESSORIES, FABRIC TEXTURE.
Make the composition look like a luxury fashion brand's professional character reference board.

PHOTOREALISM & QUALITY LOCK

Ultra-photorealistic photography, realistic skin pores, natural facial details, authentic fabric physics, precise garment construction, realistic hands, correct anatomy, sharp focus, premium studio photography, cinematic contrast, refined neutral color grading, exceptional fine detail.

Avoid plastic skin, artificial facial features, excessive beauty retouching, cartoon rendering, duplicated body parts, inconsistent faces, distorted hands, incorrect clothing, random accessories, altered colors, inconsistent hairstyles, and different identities between panels.

RESOLUTION LOCK

Generate the final image in the highest available resolution with a 16:9 aspect ratio. Preserve fine facial details, realistic fabric texture, sharp panel separation, and professional lookbook quality.

RESOLUTION LOCK: Generate final images in 16K resolution — 15360 × 8640 pixels (≈132.7 million pixels), 16:9 aspect ratio.

If the tool cannot produce native 16K output, generate at its highest supported resolution and upscale afterward without changing the character's identity or outfit.

FINAL INSTRUCTION

The uploaded reference image is the single source of truth for the character's identity, appearance, outfit, and styling.

Create ONE complete, premium, multi-panel professional character sheet featuring the exact same person in front, side, and back views, together with facial close-ups and outfit-detail photography.

Do not generate multiple unrelated characters. Do not create a new face. Do not change the original outfit.

FINAL RESULT: A cohesive, photorealistic, luxury fashion character reference sheet suitable for AI image generation, image-to-video workflows, cinematic filmmaking, fashion campaigns, and consistent character production.

EMNLP 2026 & ArabicNLP 2026 | Budapest
 
Building AI that can communicate naturally, understand multimodal content, and respect linguistic and cultural diversity remains an important research challenge.
This year at EMNLP 2026 and ArabicNLP 2026, we have several papers spanning conversational AI, speech resources, multilingual meme understanding, Arabic content safety, and culturally grounded multimodal evaluation.

Here is a quick overview of our work. If you are attending please stop by and learn more about our work.

🔹 EMNLP 2026 - Main Conference
 
1. MENASpeechBank: A Reference Voice Bank with Persona-Conditioned Multi-Turn Conversations for SpeechLLMs
How can we build speech models that support natural, diverse, persona-grounded conversations? We introduce a reference speech bank with nearly 18K utterances and over 416K persona-conditioned multi-turn conversations across Arabic varieties and English.
📅 October 26 | 11:00 - 12:30 | Poster Session D, Hall H
 📄 Paper: https://t.co/JtqNbDpmNL 
 🤗 Dataset: https://t.co/HqxKg2Kdkb

2. MemeLens: Multilingual Multitask VLMs for Memes
Memes communicate meaning through images, language, humour, and cultural context. MemeLens explores unified multilingual and multitask vision-language modelling across diverse meme understanding tasks.
📅 October 27 | 09:00 - 10:30 | Poster Session F, Hall H
 📄 Paper: https://t.co/266FDVH2Jn
 🤗 Dataset: https://t.co/sQE6Vfyzjp

3. Multi-turn Conversational AI from Text to Multimodal Interaction: Data, Models, Evaluation, and Open Challenges
What does it take for AI to maintain coherent conversations across multiple turns and modalities? Our survey examines the evolution from text dialogue to multimodal conversational systems, highlighting challenges in memory, grounding, interaction, and evaluation.
📅 October 27 | 09:00 - 10:30 | Poster Session F, Hall H
 📄 Paper: https://t.co/d8qGhrnzZ3 
 💻 Research repository: https://t.co/Yo7kbeHp4X

🔹 ArabicNLP 2026 - October 28

4. AHA-Memes: A Fine-Grained Multimodal Benchmark for Hate Detection in Arabic Memes
Detecting hate in Arabic memes requires understanding more than text alone. We introduce a fine-grained benchmark with 5K manually annotated memes and over 66K additional silver-labelled examples.
📅 October 28
📄 Paper: https://t.co/MJkRobBS4Y 
 🤗 Dataset: https://t.co/HiRzco8oPu

5. ArGuard Shared Task: Harmful Content Detection in Arabic Memes and LLM Prompts
How well can AI identify harmful content across Arabic memes and potentially unsafe LLM prompts? ArGuard brings together the community to benchmark Arabic multimodal hate detection and LLM safety.
📅 October 28
📄 Paper: https://t.co/3N675bk58p 
 🤗 Meme dataset: https://t.co/ItKKtbLa85
 💻 Shared-task resources: https://t.co/E13Br12i9t

6. ImageEval 2026: Culturally Grounded Arabic Multimodal Evaluation
Can multimodal AI truly understand cultural context? ImageEval evaluates spoken visual question answering, image-grounded hallucination detection, and cultural accuracy in image generation.
📅 October 28
📄 Paper: https://t.co/gc7r4NkIHe 
 🤗 Dataset: https://t.co/Hrhmu9qUcB

Across these projects, our goal is to develop and share resources, benchmarks, and models that help make AI more conversational, multilingual, culturally aware, and trustworthy.
Many thanks to our collaborators, students, and co-authors across institutions for their contributions.

Multi-objective protein optimization via modular diffusion steering

1 MODS is a modular framework that turns multi-objective protein design into inference-time steering of a fixed pretrained diffusion model, aiming to recover diverse Pareto tradeoffs under tight experimental-style budgets (few batched rounds).

2 Key idea: for each candidate proposal, MODS samples (a) augmented Chebyshev scalarization weights and (b) one member from a surrogate ensemble, combining them into a single scalar reward used for steering. Weight sampling explores different objective preferences; ensemble-member sampling explores predictive uncertainty.

3 The scalarization uses an augmented Chebyshev form: it emphasizes improving the worst-performing (weighted) objective while still rewarding progress on the others, helping recover tradeoffs on non-convex Pareto fronts where simple weighted sums can fail.

4 MODS separates “what to optimize” (multi-objective acquisition via scalar rewards) from “how to generate” (diffusion model + steering method). This makes the approach plug-and-play with different diffusion priors and compatible steering procedures.

5 Optimization loop: start with an initial evaluated set (100 sequences), then iterate 8 rounds of batched acquisition (100 sequences/round). After each round, MODS retrains only the fitness surrogate ensemble on accumulated observations, and reuses the same pretrained diffusion generator (no generator fine-tuning).

6 Implementations tested: two diffusion priors (MDLM masked diffusion LM; D3PM discrete diffusion) and two steering procedures (Classifier Guidance, CG; Decoupled Annealing Posterior Sampling, DAPS). Main comparisons focus on DAPS because it performed best across tasks.

7 Evaluation spans six assay-derived oracle benchmarks (5 two-objective tasks: GB1, ERBIN-PDZ1, NHERF3-PDZ2, KRAS, Src; 1 three-objective task: NHERF3-PDZ1). Oracles are CNN ensembles trained on experimental assay datasets with a distance-based penalty to discourage overconfident extrapolation far from labeled mutational neighborhoods.

8 Results: across all tasks, MODS improves substantially over unsteered sampling from the same diffusion model, and is competitive or best versus iterative baselines (ARLM+DPO, LaMBO-2, SAGE-Prot). In Table 1, MODS achieves the top mean final hypervolume on 5/6 tasks with D3PM+DAPS, and is close to the best baseline on Src with MDLM+DAPS.

9 Practical insight: steering strength matters. Too-weak regularization (oversteering away from the diffusion prior) can hurt on some tasks, consistent with reliance on less reliable surrogate predictions; the optimal setting depends jointly on task, diffusion prior, and steering procedure.

📜Paper: https://t.co/VSPsuiZkyU

CHATGPT WASN’T JUST TRAINED TO PREDICT WORDS.

IT WAS ALSO TRAINED TO LEARN WHAT HUMANS PREFER.

That’s where RLHF comes in.

Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback.

Here’s the idea:

Give an AI the same question.

It produces two different answers.

Humans compare them and choose which one is better.

Those preferences become training data.

Then:

1. HUMAN FEEDBACK
People rank competing AI responses.

2. REWARD MODEL
A model learns to predict which responses humans would prefer.

3. REINFORCEMENT LEARNING
The AI is optimized to produce responses that score better under that learned reward.

The result?

The model becomes better aligned with the preferences represented in its training feedback.

But there’s a catch.

The reward model is only a proxy for human judgment.

If it rewards the wrong things, the AI can learn to produce answers that score well without actually being better.

That’s why preference data, reward modeling, and evaluation all matter.

The big idea:

Pretraining teaches a model patterns in data.

RLHF helps shape how it responds.

AI alignment isn't just about making models smarter.

It's also about teaching them which responses humans prefer.

I have been trying to use AI agents to transact on @zomato, @Uber_India and @letsblinkit. Lots of friction. Until agents can show these marketplaces' catalogs and inventory as generative UI, user experience will be far from ideal. 

My bet: horizontal personal agents will win the long tail / low-frequency use cases, like buying insurance, an obscure brand, or a chair etc

But every high-frequency apps like ride-hailing, food, fashion etc will have its own agent on @WhatsApp. 

In the mobile era, you had a home screen full of apps. In the AI era, you will have a WhatsApp full of agents.
